from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup the scene
        lecture_lines = [
            "Meet our robot needing exact fuel amounts.",
            "It must reach a target using two thrusters.",
            "This is a system of linear equations."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Introduction: The Mixing Robot Mystery", lecture_lines)
        
        # Colors
        color_robot = WHITE
        color_target = "#00FF00"
        color_v1 = "#FF00FF"
        color_v2 = "#00FFFF"
        color_eq = WHITE
        color_highlight = "#FFFF00"

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Show a robot icon or point at the origin in #FFFFFF.
        
        # Define the coordinate plane
        # x-range to cover origin to target (7, 11)
        plane = NumberPlane(
            x_range=[-1, 9, 2],
            y_range=[-1, 13, 2],
            x_length=5,
            y_length=5,
            axis_config={"include_tip": True, "color": GREY},
            background_line_style={"stroke_opacity": 0.2}
        )
        self.place_in_area(plane, 'A1', 'F6')
        
        # Robot icon (Simple representation at origin)
        robot = Dot(plane.coords_to_point(0, 0), color=color_robot, radius=0.1)
        robot_label = Text("Robot", font_size=16, color=color_robot).next_to(robot, DL, buff=0.1)

        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(color_robot))
        self.play(Create(plane), FadeIn(robot, robot_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Display target vector b = [7, 11] in #00FF00.
        # Display thruster vectors v1 = [2, 1] in #FF00FF and v2 = [1, 3] in #00FFFF.

        b_vec = Arrow(plane.coords_to_point(0, 0), plane.coords_to_point(7, 11), buff=0, color=color_target, stroke_width=4)
        b_label = MathTex("\\vec{b}", color=color_target).scale(0.8).next_to(b_vec.get_end(), UR, buff=0.1)
        
        v1_vec = Arrow(plane.coords_to_point(0, 0), plane.coords_to_point(2, 1), buff=0, color=color_v1, stroke_width=4)
        v1_label = MathTex("\\vec{v}_1", color=color_v1).scale(0.8).next_to(v1_vec.get_end(), RIGHT, buff=0.1)
        
        v2_vec = Arrow(plane.coords_to_point(0, 0), plane.coords_to_point(1, 3), buff=0, color=color_v2, stroke_width=4)
        v2_label = MathTex("\\vec{v}_2", color=color_v2).scale(0.8).next_to(v2_vec.get_end(), UP, buff=0.1)

        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(color_target))
        self.play(GrowArrow(b_vec), Write(b_label))
        self.play(GrowArrow(v1_vec), Write(v1_label), GrowArrow(v2_vec), Write(v2_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Animate the equation x*v1 + y*v2 = b appearing in #FFFFFF.
        # Highlight the unknowns x and y with #FFFF00.
        
        # Placing the equation near the top (using grid system for major positioning)
        eq = MathTex("x", "\\vec{v}_1", "+", "y", "\\vec{v}_2", "=", "\\vec{b}", color=color_eq)
        self.place_at_grid(eq, 'A3', scale_factor=0.9)
        
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(color_highlight))
        self.play(Write(eq))
        self.wait(0.5)
        
        # Highlight x and y
        self.play(
            eq[0].animate.set_color(color_highlight),
            eq[3].animate.set_color(color_highlight)
        )
        self.wait(2)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup the layout with section title and lecture lines
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite: Determinant as Area", [
            "Determinants measure the area of a parallelogram.",
            "Two vectors form the sides of this shape.",
            "If the area is zero, the grid collapses."
        ])

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Show unit square formed by [1, 0] and [0, 1] in #FFFFFF.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        
        # Create and position a coordinate system
        plane = NumberPlane(
            x_range=[-1, 5], 
            y_range=[-1, 5], 
            x_length=4.5, 
            y_length=4.5,
            background_line_style={"stroke_color": GREY, "stroke_opacity": 0.4}
        )
        self.place_in_area(plane, "A1", "F6", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        # Unit square defined at the origin of the plane
        square = Polygon(
            plane.c2p(0, 0), plane.c2p(1, 0), plane.c2p(1, 1), plane.c2p(0, 1), 
            color=WHITE, fill_opacity=0.2
        )
        v1_unit = Arrow(plane.c2p(0, 0), plane.c2p(1, 0), buff=0, color=WHITE, stroke_width=4)
        v2_unit = Arrow(plane.c2p(0, 0), plane.c2p(0, 1), buff=0, color=WHITE, stroke_width=4)
        
        self.play(
            Create(plane),
            DrawBorderThenFill(square),
            GrowArrow(v1_unit),
            GrowArrow(v2_unit),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Transform square into parallelogram using v1 = [2, 1] and v2 = [1, 3] in #00FFFF.
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#00FFFF")
        
        # Target coordinates for vectors v1 and v2
        v1_target_coords = [2, 1, 0]
        v2_target_coords = [1, 3, 0]
        v12_sum_coords = [3, 4, 0] # v1 + v2

        # Create the parallelogram and target arrows in cyan
        parallelogram = Polygon(
            plane.c2p(0, 0), 
            plane.c2p(*v1_target_coords), 
            plane.c2p(*v12_sum_coords), 
            plane.c2p(*v2_target_coords), 
            color="#00FFFF", 
            fill_opacity=0.5
        )
        v1_target_arrow = Arrow(plane.c2p(0, 0), plane.c2p(*v1_target_coords), buff=0, color="#00FFFF", stroke_width=4)
        v2_target_arrow = Arrow(plane.c2p(0, 0), plane.c2p(*v2_target_coords), buff=0, color="#00FFFF", stroke_width=4)
        
        # Label for the determinant
        det_label = MathTex(r"\text{det}(A)", color="#00FFFF").scale(0.8)
        # Position label inside the parallelogram area
        det_label.move_to(parallelogram.get_center())
        
        self.play(
            Transform(square, parallelogram),
            Transform(v1_unit, v1_target_arrow),
            Transform(v2_unit, v2_target_arrow),
            Write(det_label),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # If the area is zero, the grid collapses.
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FF5555")
        
        # Collapsed state: v2 is collinear with v1 (v2 = 0.5 * v1)
        v2_col_coords = [1, 0.5, 0]
        v12_col_sum = [3, 1.5, 0]
        
        collapsed_poly = Polygon(
            plane.c2p(0, 0), 
            plane.c2p(*v1_target_coords), 
            plane.c2p(*v12_col_sum), 
            plane.c2p(*v2_col_coords), 
            color="#FF5555", 
            fill_opacity=0.8
        )
        v2_col_arrow = Arrow(plane.c2p(0, 0), plane.c2p(*v2_col_coords), buff=0, color="#FF5555", stroke_width=4)
        
        det_label_zero = MathTex(r"\text{det}(A) = 0", color="#FF5555").scale(0.8)
        # Move label near the collapsed line
        det_label_zero.move_to(plane.c2p(3, 0.5, 0))

        self.play(
            Transform(square, collapsed_poly),
            Transform(v2_unit, v2_col_arrow),
            v1_unit.animate.set_color("#FF5555"),
            Transform(det_label, det_label_zero),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Data for vectors
        v1_color = "#FF00FF"
        v2_color = "#00FFFF"
        b_color = "#00FF00"
        
        v1_coords = np.array([2, 1, 0])
        v2_coords = np.array([1, 3, 0])
        b_coords = np.array([7, 11, 0])
        
        # Solving x*v1 + y*v2 = b
        # 2x + 1y = 7
        # 1x + 3y = 11 -> x = 2, y = 3
        x_scale = 2
        y_scale = 3

        lecture_lines = [
            "We scale vectors to reach our target point.",
            "Finding x and y means finding these scales.",
            "It's like navigating a custom, skewed grid."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Linear Combination Visual", lecture_lines)

        # Coordinate Plane Setup
        # We need to fit b=[7, 11]. x_range=[-1, 9], y_range=[-1, 13]
        plane = NumberPlane(
            x_range=[-1, 9, 2],
            y_range=[-1, 13, 2],
            x_length=5,
            y_length=5,
            background_line_style={"stroke_opacity": 0.4},
            axis_config={"include_numbers": True, "font_size": 16}
        )
        self.place_in_area(plane, "A1", "F6")
        
        # Origin position for vectors
        origin = plane.coords_to_point(0, 0)
        
        v1 = Vector(plane.coords_to_point(*v1_coords) - origin, color=v1_color)
        v1.shift(origin)
        v1_label = MathTex("v_1", color=v1_color, font_size=24).next_to(v1.get_end(), RIGHT, buff=0.1)
        
        v2 = Vector(plane.coords_to_point(*v2_coords) - origin, color=v2_color)
        v2.shift(origin)
        v2_label = MathTex("v_2", color=v2_color, font_size=24).next_to(v2.get_end(), LEFT, buff=0.1)

        b_vec = Vector(plane.coords_to_point(*b_coords) - origin, color=b_color)
        b_vec.shift(origin)
        b_label = MathTex("b", color=b_color, font_size=24).next_to(b_vec.get_end(), UP, buff=0.1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.play(Create(plane), run_time=1)
        self.play(GrowArrow(v1), Write(v1_label))
        self.play(GrowArrow(v2), Write(v2_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(YELLOW)
        )
        
        # Target vector b
        self.play(GrowArrow(b_vec), Write(b_label))
        self.wait(0.5)
        
        # Scaling v1 and v2
        scaled_v1_coords = x_scale * v1_coords
        scaled_v2_coords = y_scale * v2_coords
        
        v1_scaled = Vector(plane.coords_to_point(*scaled_v1_coords) - origin, color=v1_color)
        v1_scaled.shift(origin)
        v1_scaled_label = MathTex(f"{x_scale}v_1", color=v1_color, font_size=24).next_to(v1_scaled.get_end(), DOWN, buff=0.1)
        
        v2_scaled = Vector(plane.coords_to_point(*scaled_v2_coords) - origin, color=v2_color)
        v2_scaled.shift(origin)
        v2_scaled_label = MathTex(f"{y_scale}v_2", color=v2_color, font_size=24).next_to(v2_scaled.get_end(), LEFT, buff=0.1)
        
        self.play(
            Transform(v1, v1_scaled),
            Transform(v1_label, v1_scaled_label),
            run_time=1.5
        )
        self.play(
            Transform(v2, v2_scaled),
            Transform(v2_label, v2_scaled_label),
            run_time=1.5
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(YELLOW)
        )
        
        # Tip-to-tail
        # Move scaled v2 to tip of scaled v1
        tip_v1 = v1.get_end()
        self.play(
            v2.animate.shift(tip_v1 - origin),
            v2_label.animate.shift(tip_v1 - origin),
            run_time=2
        )
        
        # Create the "skewed grid" lines
        grid_lines = VGroup()
        # Add a few lines in v1 and v2 directions
        for i in range(5):
            # Lines parallel to v1
            start1 = plane.coords_to_point(*(i * v2_coords))
            end1 = plane.coords_to_point(*(i * v2_coords + 4 * v1_coords))
            grid_lines.add(Line(start1, end1, color=v1_color, stroke_width=1, stroke_opacity=0.3))
            
            # Lines parallel to v2
            start2 = plane.coords_to_point(*(i * v1_coords))
            end2 = plane.coords_to_point(*(i * v1_coords + 4 * v2_coords))
            grid_lines.add(Line(start2, end2, color=v2_color, stroke_width=1, stroke_opacity=0.3))
        
        self.play(Create(grid_lines), run_time=2)
        self.wait(2)
        
        # Cleanup
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        self.wait(1)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Title and Lecture Lines
        lines = [
            "Replace one column with the target vector.",
            "This creates a new, sliding parallelogram area.",
            "Adding a multiple of another vector shears it.",
            "Shearing doesn't change the area's base or height.",
            "So, the new area is x times the original."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Geometric Trick: The 'Sliding' Area", lines)

        # Colors
        COLOR_V1V2 = "#00FFFF" # Cyan
        COLOR_B = "#FF00FF"    # Magenta
        COLOR_TEXT = "#FFFFFF" # White
        COLOR_DECOMP = "#FFFF00" # Yellow

        # Define vectors based on x*v1 + y*v2 = b
        # Let x=2, y=3, v1=[2, 1], v2=[1, 3] -> b = [7, 11]
        v1_val = np.array([2, 1, 0])
        v2_val = np.array([1, 3, 0])
        x_val, y_val = 2.0, 3.0
        b_val = x_val * v1_val + y_val * v2_val # [7, 11]
        
        # Scale for grid visualization
        plot_scale = 0.22
        
        def to_plot(vec):
            return vec * plot_scale

        # Origin point on the grid
        plot_origin = self.grid["F2"] # Bottom-left of the right grid area
        
        def get_pos(vec):
            return plot_origin + to_plot(vec)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 0 ===
        # Replace one column with the target vector.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        v1_arr = Arrow(plot_origin, get_pos(v1_val), buff=0, color=COLOR_V1V2, stroke_width=4)
        v2_arr = Arrow(plot_origin, get_pos(v2_val), buff=0, color=COLOR_V1V2, stroke_width=4)
        v1_lab = MathTex("v_1", color=COLOR_V1V2, font_size=24).next_to(v1_arr.get_end(), RIGHT, buff=0.1)
        v2_lab = MathTex("v_2", color=COLOR_V1V2, font_size=24).next_to(v2_arr.get_end(), UP, buff=0.1)
        
        # Original Parallelogram (v1, v2)
        p_orig = Polygon(
            plot_origin, get_pos(v1_val), get_pos(v1_val + v2_val), get_pos(v2_val),
            stroke_width=2, stroke_color=COLOR_V1V2, fill_color=COLOR_V1V2, fill_opacity=0.3
        )
        
        self.play(Create(v1_arr), Create(v2_arr), Write(v1_lab), Write(v2_lab))
        self.play(Create(p_orig))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # This creates a new, sliding parallelogram area.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        b_arr = Arrow(plot_origin, get_pos(b_val), buff=0, color=COLOR_B, stroke_width=4)
        b_lab = MathTex("b", color=COLOR_B, font_size=24).next_to(b_arr.get_end(), RIGHT, buff=0.1)
        
        # New Parallelogram (b, v2)
        p_new = Polygon(
            plot_origin, get_pos(b_val), get_pos(b_val + v2_val), get_pos(v2_val),
            stroke_width=2, stroke_color=COLOR_B, fill_color=COLOR_B, fill_opacity=0.3
        )
        
        self.play(Create(b_arr), Write(b_lab))
        self.play(FadeIn(p_new))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Adding a multiple of another vector shears it.
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Show b = x*v1 + y*v2
        b_eq = MathTex("b = x v_1 + y v_2", color=COLOR_TEXT, font_size=32)
        self.place_at_grid(b_eq, "A4")
        
        x_v1_vec = x_val * v1_val
        y_v2_vec = y_val * v2_val
        
        # Visual decomposition
        x_v1_arr = Arrow(plot_origin, get_pos(x_v1_vec), buff=0, color=ORANGE, stroke_width=3)
        y_v2_arr = Arrow(get_pos(x_v1_vec), get_pos(b_val), buff=0, color=COLOR_DECOMP, stroke_width=3)
        
        x_v1_lab = MathTex("x v_1", color=ORANGE, font_size=22).next_to(x_v1_arr.get_center(), DOWN, buff=0.1)
        y_v2_lab = MathTex("y v_2", color=COLOR_DECOMP, font_size=22).next_to(y_v2_arr.get_center(), RIGHT, buff=0.1)
        
        self.play(Write(b_eq))
        self.play(Create(x_v1_arr), Create(y_v2_arr), Write(x_v1_lab), Write(y_v2_lab))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Shearing doesn't change the area's base or height.
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[3].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Sliding mechanism using a ValueTracker to move the tip from b to x*v1
        slide_tracker = ValueTracker(0)
        
        # The parallelogram that updates its shape
        moving_p = p_new.copy()
        
        def update_p(p):
            t = slide_tracker.get_value()
            # Transition from b to x*v1
            current_tip = b_val - t * y_v2_vec
            p.set_points_as_corners([
                plot_origin, 
                get_pos(current_tip), 
                get_pos(current_tip + v2_val), 
                get_pos(v2_val),
                plot_origin
            ])
            
        moving_p.add_updater(update_p)
        self.add(moving_p)
        self.remove(p_new)
        
        # Note: sliding along v2 direction means height is constant
        guide_line = DashedLine(get_pos(b_val), get_pos(x_v1_vec), color=WHITE, stroke_width=1)
        self.play(Create(guide_line))
        self.play(slide_tracker.animate.set_value(1), run_time=3)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # So, the new area is x times the original.
        self.lecture[3].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[4].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        final_eq = MathTex(
            "Area(b, v_2) = x \\cdot Area(v_1, v_2)",
            color=COLOR_TEXT, font_size=32
        )
        self.place_at_grid(final_eq, "B4")
        
        # Show that final shape is x times the original along the v1 direction
        # Since x=2, we show two copies of the original parallelogram
        p_chunk1 = p_orig.copy().set_fill(opacity=0.6).set_stroke(width=4)
        p_chunk2 = Polygon(
            get_pos(v1_val), get_pos(2*v1_val), get_pos(2*v1_val + v2_val), get_pos(v1_val + v2_val),
            stroke_width=4, stroke_color=COLOR_V1V2, fill_color=COLOR_V1V2, fill_opacity=0.6
        )
        
        self.play(Write(final_eq))
        self.play(FadeIn(p_chunk1))
        self.play(FadeIn(p_chunk2))
        self.play(Indicate(final_eq))
        self.wait(2)

class TeachingScene(Scene):

        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)

        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)

        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2

class Section6Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Initial Setup
        title = "Summary and Real-World Intuition"
        lines = [
            "Solve equations by comparing geometric areas.",
            "The rule fails if the base area is zero.",
            "Geometry reveals the logic behind the algebra."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Grid Coordinates for Visualization
        # We'll use a small coordinate system in the right area
        # Origin at D2
        origin = self.grid["D2"]
        scale_map = 0.25
        
        def to_scene_coords(vec):
            return origin + np.array([vec[0]*scale_map, vec[1]*scale_map, 0])

        # Vectors: v1=[2,1], v2=[1,3], b=[7,11], solution x=2, y=3
        v1 = np.array([2, 1, 0])
        v2 = np.array([1, 3, 0])
        b_vec = np.array([7, 11, 0])
        
        # Elements
        axes_x = Arrow(to_scene_coords([-1, 0]), to_scene_coords([8, 0]), color=GRAY, stroke_width=2, buff=0)
        axes_y = Arrow(to_scene_coords([0, -1]), to_scene_coords([0, 12]), color=GRAY, stroke_width=2, buff=0)
        
        target_b = Dot(to_scene_coords(b_vec), color="#00FF00")
        label_b = MathTex("b", color="#00FF00", font_size=24).next_to(target_b, UR, buff=0.1)
        
        # Robot (represented as a circle)
        robot = Circle(radius=0.1, color=WHITE, fill_opacity=1).move_to(to_scene_coords([0,0]))
        
        self.play(Create(axes_x), Create(axes_y))
        self.play(FadeIn(target_b), Write(label_b))
        self.play(FadeIn(robot))
        
        # Move robot along x*v1 and y*v2
        path_x = Line(to_scene_coords([0,0]), to_scene_coords(2*v1), color="#FF00FF")
        path_y = Line(to_scene_coords(2*v1), to_scene_coords(2*v1 + 3*v2), color="#00FFFF")
        
        self.play(robot.animate.move_to(to_scene_coords(2*v1)), Create(path_x), run_time=1.5)
        self.play(robot.animate.move_to(to_scene_coords(b_vec)), Create(path_y), run_time=1.5)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Clear path, keep target and robot for context
        self.play(FadeOut(path_x), FadeOut(path_y), robot.animate.move_to(to_scene_coords([0,0])))
        
        # Show Determinant Collapsing
        # Start with standard v1, v2
        vec1 = Vector(to_scene_coords(v1) - origin, color="#FF00FF").shift(origin)
        vec2 = Vector(to_scene_coords(v2) - origin, color="#00FFFF").shift(origin)
        
        # Parallelogram
        p_points = [
            to_scene_coords([0,0]),
            to_scene_coords(v1),
            to_scene_coords(v1+v2),
            to_scene_coords(v2)
        ]
        parallelogram = Polygon(*p_points, color=BLUE, fill_opacity=0.3)
        
        det_text = MathTex("det(A)", color=WHITE, font_size=24)
        self.place_at_grid(det_text, "B5")

        self.play(Create(vec1), Create(vec2), FadeIn(parallelogram))
        self.play(Write(det_text))
        self.wait(0.5)
        
        # Collapse: make v2 parallel to v1
        v2_new = np.array([4, 2, 0]) # linearly dependent (2 * v1)
        
        new_vec2_end = to_scene_coords(v2_new)
        new_p_points = [
            to_scene_coords([0,0]),
            to_scene_coords(v1),
            to_scene_coords(v1+v2_new),
            to_scene_coords(v2_new)
        ]
        
        det_zero = MathTex("det(A) = 0", color=RED, font_size=32)
        self.place_at_grid(det_zero, "B5")

        self.play(
            vec2.animate.put_start_and_end_on(origin, new_vec2_end),
            parallelogram.animate.set_points_as_corners(new_p_points),
            Transform(det_text, det_zero),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(1.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Fade out geometry
        self.play(
            FadeOut(vec1), FadeOut(vec2), FadeOut(parallelogram), 
            FadeOut(det_text), FadeOut(axes_x), FadeOut(axes_y),
            FadeOut(target_b), FadeOut(label_b), FadeOut(robot)
        )
        
        # Show final solved coordinates
        final_coords = MathTex("(x, y) = (2, 3)", color=WHITE, font_size=48)
        self.place_in_area(final_coords, "B2", "E5")
        
        self.play(Write(final_coords))
        self.wait(2)
        
        # Final cleanup
        self.play(FadeOut(final_coords), FadeOut(self.title), FadeOut(self.lecture))
        self.wait(1)

outline.topic: The Geometry of Cramer's Rule: Why Areas Solve Equations
outline.target_audience: Undergraduate students in Linear Algebra or advanced high school students

sections.title: Introduction: The Mixing Robot Mystery
sections.content: Introduce a scenario where a 'Resource Allocation Robot' needs to find the exact amounts of two fuel types (x and y) to reach a specific target location (vector b). Frame the problem as a system of linear equations Ax = b, but instead of using algebra, we will use 'spatial intuition'.
sections.example: A robot needs to reach point (7, 11) using two directional thrusters: Thruster A [2, 1] and Thruster B [1, 3]. How much of each thruster do we need?

sections.title: Prerequisite: Determinant as Area
sections.content: Visually demonstrate that the determinant of a 2x2 matrix represents the signed area of the parallelogram formed by its column vectors. If the area is zero, the 'grid' has collapsed.
sections.example: Show a unit square [1,0] and [0,1] being transformed by matrix A into a parallelogram. The area of this new shape is det(A).

sections.title: The Linear Combination Visual
sections.content: Show that the equation x*v1 + y*v2 = b means scaling the first column vector (v1) by x and the second (v2) by y to reach the target vector b. Highlight that finding x and y is like finding the 'coordinates' in a skewed grid.
sections.example: An animation showing vector v1 stretching by a factor of 'x' and v2 stretching by 'y' to tip-to-tail reach vector b.

sections.title: The Geometric Trick: The 'Sliding' Area
sections.content: Introduce the core insight: If we replace the first column of the matrix with vector b, the area of the resulting parallelogram is exactly x times the original area. This is because adding a multiple of one vector to another (shear) doesn't change the area, but scaling one side does.
sections.example: Visualize a parallelogram formed by (x*v1 + y*v2) and v2. Since y*v2 is parallel to v2, it contributes nothing to the 'height' or area relative to v2. Thus, Area(b, v2) = Area(x*v1, v2) = x * Area(v1, v2).

sections.title: Deriving the Rule: The Ratio of Areas
sections.content: Conclude that since Area(b, v2) = x * Area(v1, v2), then x must be the ratio of the modified area to the original area. This is Cramer's Rule: x = det(Ab)/det(A). Repeat the logic for y by replacing the second column.
sections.example: A split-screen animation showing the 'Target Area' (with b) being divided by the 'Base Area' to reveal the scalar value of x.

sections.title: Summary and Real-World Intuition
sections.content: Recap the flow: System of equations -> Parallelogram areas -> Ratio of areas = Solution. Explain why this fails when det(A)=0 (the area is zero, so you can't divide).
sections.example: The Robot successfully reaches point (7, 11) by calculating the ratio of two shaded regions on its digital map.

[section_1] Implement Manim code for the Introduction. 
1. Display target vector b = [7, 11] in #00FF00.
2. Display thruster vectors v1 = [2, 1] in #FF00FF and v2 = [1, 3] in #00FFFF.
3. Show a robot icon or point at the origin in #FFFFFF.
4. Animate the equation x*v1 + y*v2 = b appearing in #FFFFFF.
5. Highlight unknowns x and y with #FFFF00.
Coordinate with Section 3 for vector consistency.
issues.resolution_note: Implemented Section 1 according to storyboard: target vector [7,11], thrusters [2,1] and [1,3], robot at origin, and equation x*v1 + y*v2 = b with x/y highlights.

issues.description:
[section_2] Implement Manim code for Determinant Prerequisite.
1. Show unit square formed by [1, 0] and [0, 1] in #FFFFFF.
2. Transform square into parallelogram using v1 = [2, 1] and v2 = [1, 3] in #00FFFF.
3. Fill parallelogram interior with #00FFFF and label it det(A).
Ensure the transformation is smooth and the label is clear.
issues.resolution_note: Implemented the determinant prerequisite animation: unit square, transform to parallelogram (v1=[2,1], v2=[1,3]), and det(A)=0 collapse.

issues.description:
[section_3] Implement Manim code for Linear Combination Visual.
1. Show vectors v1 = [2, 1] and v2 = [1, 3] on a coordinate plane in #FF00FF and #00FFFF.
2. Animate v1 scaling by x and v2 scaling by y to reach b = [7, 11].
3. Connect scaled vectors tip-to-tail to reach target b in #00FF00.
This section sets the stage for the geometric trick in Section 4.
issues.resolution_note: Implemented the linear combination visual: v1=[2,1], v2=[1,3], b=[7,11], with scaling factors x=2, y=3. Included tip-to-tail animation and a skewed grid overlay.

issues.description:
[section_4] Implement Manim code for The Geometric Trick.
1. Show original parallelogram (v1, v2) in #00FFFF.
2. Overlay a new parallelogram (b, v2) in #FF00FF, where b = [7, 11] and v2 = [1, 3].
3. Express b as x*v1 + y*v2 near the vectors in #FFFFFF.
4. Show y*v2 part of b 'sliding' along v2 direction, maintaining area.
5. Highlight that the new area (b, v2) is x * original area (v1, v2).
This is the core conceptual animation. Ensure the 'sliding' (shearing) is visually intuitive.
issues.resolution_note: Implemented the 'sliding' area animation. Used v1=[2,1], v2=[1,3], b=[7,11] to demonstrate b=2v1+3v2. Animated the shearing process and showed the resulting area is exactly x times the original.

issues.description:
[section_5] Implement Manim code for Cramer's Rule Derivation.
1. Display the ratio x = Area(b, v2) / Area(v1, v2) in #FFFFFF.
2. Show Area(b, v2) as the determinant of matrix A_1 in #FF00FF.
3. Display the ratio y = Area(v1, b) / Area(v1, v2) in #FFFFFF.
4. Show Area(v1, b) as the determinant of matrix A_2 in #00FFFF.
5. Highlight the common denominator det(A) in both formulas in #FFFF00.
Use split-screen or sequential display to show the derivation for both x and y.
issues.resolution_note: Implemented Section 5 Manim code with Cramer's Rule derivation (x and y ratios, determinants, and common denominator highlight). Followed the 6x6 grid system and color constraints.

issues.description:
[section_6] Implement Manim code for Summary.
1. Show the robot successfully reaching the target b = [7, 11] in #00FF00.
2. Display det(A) = 0 and show the parallelogram collapsing to a line to explain failure.
3. Fade out with the final solved coordinates (x, y) in #FFFFFF.
Ensure a satisfying conclusion to the robot narrative.
issues.resolution_note: Generated Manim code for Section 6 following the storyboard and orchestral requirements.
